mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong labor market growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the effect inverts during periods of rising wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong export growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases uncertainty and reduces equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed when unemployment falls sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both decline > 1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the effect is absent during periods of strong credit expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE but rising PAYEMS) above 62% for four consecutive months signals improved labor supply without wage inflation, which supports corporate profit margins and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable and PAYEMS rising for 4 consecutive months with LFPR > 62%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of accelerating wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio above historical median for six months) signals elevated precautionary savings and lower marginal propensity to consume, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS/GDPC1 > historical median for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong fiscal stimulus.
